title: Constructors and Member Initialization
learningObjectives: Write constructors for explicit object initialization.
Understand initialization order follows declaration order.
Initialize const and reference members correctly.
Prefer valid state from the moment an object is created.

understand.concept: A constructor initializes an object when it is created. Member initializer lists initialize members directly in declaration order, which is the actual order regardless of list order.
understand.whyItMatters: Constructors help ensure objects begin in a valid state.
understand.explain: Initialize every member, prefer initializer lists, and note that const/reference members must be initialized.

examples.title: Constructor initializes fields
examples.code: class Point{public:Point(int a,int b):x(a),y(b){}int x,y;};\nPoint p(3,4);
examples.explanation: The initializer list initializes members before the constructor body.

examples.title: Default constructor
examples.explanation: Constructor gives the object a defined starting state.

examples.title: Default member and constructor
examples.explanation: Member initializer list constructs the string member.

examples.title: Initializer declaration order
examples.explanation: Members initialize in declaration order (first then second), not list order.

examples.title: Const member initialized
examples.code: class Ticket{public:Ticket(int n):id(n){}int getId()const{return id;}private:const int id;};
examples.explanation: A const data member must be initialized in the initializer list.

practise.guidedTask: For Constructors and Member Initialization, trace every example. List each type, object, member, initial value, access path, and state change. Identify where encapsulation or initialization affects correctness.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ model focused on Constructors and Member Initialization (such as a Point, Student, Product, or Account). Include multiple objects, initialization, at least one operation/member access, and test normal, boundary and invalid states. Explain which fields should be public or private and why.
hints: Define the type and its responsibilities before creating objects.
Initialize members deliberately and trace their values.
Use dot for objects and arrow only for pointers.
Keep fields private when they must enforce rules.
Test object creation, valid operations and rejected updates.

questions.explanation: Const members must be initialized at construction.
